name: RKC Plank
research: Prone forearm plank, long lever (NSCA S2). Elbow interior ~100 deg -> forearm flat toward the head, upper arm tilted 10 deg past vertical toward the feet: elbow 0.269*sin10 = 0.047 m ahead of the shoulder; elbows ~0.15 m apart (x +-0.075) vs shoulders +-0.22 -> dx -0.145; vertical h = sqrt(0.269^2-0.145^2-0.047^2) = 0.222; shoulder z = 0.222 + 0.045 = 0.267. Ankles on the toes z 0.165 (foot rot 70: ball ~0.157 under the ankle). Body line rise 0.102 over 1.37 m -> 4.3 deg -> torso at rot X 85.7: shoulder offset z -0.041 -> root z 0.308. Posterior tilt: pelvis root rot 80.7 (5 deg 'lean back' of the pelvis), spine05 +3 / spine04 +2 bring the trunk back onto the 85.7 line. Upper arm direction world (-0.539,-0.175,-0.825) -> torso (-0.539,0.836,0.113) -> elev 96.5, plane 123 (forward and inward). Elbow bend 80 (= interior 100) with bend_world -Y makes the forearm horizontal: check fore = du cos80 + bperp sin80 = (0.001,-1.0,0.001). Fists thumb-up: axis = world up in the torso frame (0,-1,0.07). Feet together: hip L (0.11,-0.011,0.258) -> ankle (0.06,0.892,0.165), hip-ankle 0.909 = locked knee. Sources S1 Schoenfeld 2014, S2 Schoenfeld & Contreras 2013 NSCA, S3 Oliva-Lozano 2020. QA 11 Nov: whole body moved by the measured lowest point so it rests on the floor (cloud run 43079162675). 13 Nov 2026 (pics-fixes): 'ground' lifts the body until the lowest forearm/fist skin is on the floor and each foot's toes touch (the old fixed numbers left the forearms 5 cm in the floor).
